Theme

Nature & food

lair noun

also den, burrow, hole (of an animal), sett, earth (of a fox), hiding place, covert, form (of a hare)

classical

Cic. ND 2.126 (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 6.27 (Lewis & Short)
Phaedr. 1.19.9 (Lewis & Short)

cubīle, cubīlis n.

noun, third declension

the resting place of an animal: lair, den, nest, burrow

A place to lie down, of people a bed; of the mouse, the dog, the elk, the mole (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • lustrum, lustrī n. — the haunt or den of wild beasts (usually plural, lustra)

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Verg. G. 2.471: lustra ferārum (Lewis & Short); Verg. A. 3.647 (Lewis & Short)

    First a muddy wallow, a bog (Varr. RR 2.4.8).

  • latebra, latebrae f. — a hiding place, a covert (usually plural, latebrae)

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 6.43: latebrīs ac silvīs aut saltibus sē ēripere (Lewis & Short); Plaut. Aul. 4.2.2 (Lewis & Short)

    From lateō, lie hidden.

Examples

  • aut oculīs captī fōdēre cubīlia talpae

    or the blind moles have dug their bedsVerg. G. 1.183

  • illīc saltūs ac lustra ferārum

    there are the woodland pastures and the lairs of wild beastsVerg. G. 2.471

  • Maenala trānsieram latebrīs horrenda ferārum

    I had crossed Maenala, bristling with the lairs of wild beastsOv. Met. 1.216

See also nest, hole, tunnel, cave, hide, wild, fox, badger.

SourcesLewis & Short: cubile · Lewis & Short: lustrum · Lewis & Short: latebra

Vergil, Georgica 1.183, 2.471. Ovid, Metamorphoses 1.216.
